watches.name: TPS Twelve
watches.description: ROUE TPS has made a commitment to revive and rewrite the subtle refinement from the 1960s racing culture, which seems to have been lost. The TPS is a tribute to the Porsche 910, winner of the Nürburgring 1000-kilometer race in 1967. This car gave Porsche the most sentimental of its victories after seven years trying an overall win in a prestigious world sports car race competition and a decade fighting for a win in Germany’s most iconic track. The homage is present in an elaborated embossed car front drawing on the screw case-back. With an interesting pulsometer calculator feature, TPS is now available in several version — each limited to 1000 pieces and individually numbered. All versions have triple-layer dial construction and Swiss Super-Luminova® printed. They all come with pre-color-set leather “Driver” and “Sports” silicone interchangeable straps.

watches.name: Cal Four
watches.description: The 1930s saw the birth of Bauhaus, modernism and, along with it, unbridled optimism. The CAL stands at this pinnacle of early Modernism design. Not coincidentally, this era’s racing phenoms made the sport’s most complex technology to date look simple, effortless, and thrilling. Streamlined cushion cases are lightweight and finished to perfection, a signature yellow-gold crystal gasket, uniquely inspired dials that incorporate multi-layered design for an eye-catching presentation. The CAL impresses for less while being comfortable on the wrist and ready for everyday wear.

watches.name: HDS Two
watches.description: The HDS Hands brings us to the 1980s where we relied heavily on inspiration from renowned functionalist Dieter Rams, a name synonymous with brutally beautiful, industrially iconic German engineering and design. The elements of the HDS offer a deft blend of German minimalist expression inspired by the best of Rams’s work for Braun. All three versions feature a bold oversized outer minutes ring surrounding two separate hours tracks – one housing clean Arabic numerals, the other line markers. The separate concentric rings give off a stepped effect, enhanced by the subtly darker gray of the outer minutes ring. Note the hands: in lieu of staid, straight pieces, we’ve tapered them, adding some contrasting curve and liveliness to the domination of straight lines. What’s more, the gasket yellow is echoed through the dial emblem and seconds hand.

watches.name: CHR Ten
watches.description: At ROUE, evolution comes from attention. The third generation of the CHR brings significant refinements to one of our most iconic models. Now with a brushed finish case, a new set of straps, including a stainless steel bracelet and a genuine leather option, and improved water resistance to 10 ATM. Each version is created with care, precision, and intention. The CHR maintains its original DNA while moving towards an even more assertive design. Available in four striking colors. Limited edition.

watches.name: SSD Two
watches.description: With its clean lines, unobtrusive profile and exquisite attention to detail, the stunning seconds sub dial SSD pays homage to the 1960s, a simpler, some might say nobler, era that produced timeless, sophisticated design. The architecture takes its inspiration from the best hand stopwatches of that period. Note the Gran Prix style bezel, common in racing watches of that time period. The lines are simple, with only a single bevel along the upper edge of the case. Deviating from the script, we’ve foregone the traditional black crystal gasket for a rich, eye-catching golden yellow, allowing the dial to take center stage. All of this is rounded out by a precision display featuring a sub-dial reminiscent of a Smiths gauge on the legendary Jaguar E-type.
